title: Annotatio IV §.XVI: Bernard’s triple — spiritual food, spiritual presence, spiritual eating by faith
pass_a_gloss: By which double utterance most sinewy he perorates the whole truth concerning Christ’s body in the Sacred Supper, (1) by making it food of the mind and therefore Spiritual food, and therefore (2) that it is present and exhibited not corporally but spiritually. Finally, (3.) what is Spiritually exhibited is therefore also eaten spiritually, because the nature and reason of eating follows the nature and reason of the food; And so, as corporal food taken corporally goes to the use of the body, so spiritual food received spiritually or by faith goes to the use of the Spirit, or of the faithful Soul — i.e. to the increase and establishment of faith and of communion with Christ. Compare Bernard’s Sermon on the Sacred Supper on John ch. 6 verse 56 (563).
pass_b_english: Bernard’s sinewy triple on the Supper: (1) food of the mind = Spiritual food; (2) present and exhibited spiritually, not corporally;

(3) therefore eaten spiritually — eating matches the food’s nature: corporal food for the body, spiritual food received by faith for the faithful soul’s increase of faith and communion with Christ (cf. John 6:56).
source_text: Quô duplici effatô nervosissimâ omnem de corpore Christi in S. Cœna veritatem perorat, (1) faciendo istud cibum mentis eóque cibum Spiritualem, quodque idcirco (2) non corporaliter, sed spiritualiter præsens sit ac exhibeatur. Denique, (3.) Spiritualiter exhibitum, spiritualiter etiam proptereà manducetur, quia naturam rationemque cibi insequatur natura & ratio manducationis; Eóque, uti cibus corporalis, corporaliter assumtus, in corporis usum, ita cibus spiritualis, spiritualiter seu fide acceptus, in usum Spiritus, seu Animæ fidelis, i. e. in augmentum ac stabilimentum fidei communionisque cum Christo concedat. Confer Sermonem Bernhardi de S. Cœna in Caput VI. Johannis versum 56. 563.
